problem: For the function $f(x,y)=y{e}^{xy}-{x}^{2}{y}^{2},$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ at the point $(1,1).$
worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $y,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the sum and constant multiple rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y{e}^{xy}-{x}^{2}{y}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y{e}^{xy})-\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}{y}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y{e}^{xy})-{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the product, the chain, and the constant multiple rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂y}(y{e}^{xy})-{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}) & =(\frac{∂}{∂y}(y)\cdot {e}^{xy}+y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{xy}))-{x}^{2}\cdot (2y) \\  & =(1\cdot {e}^{xy}+y\cdot {e}^{xy}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(xy))-2{x}^{2}y \\  & =({e}^{xy}+y\cdot {e}^{xy}\cdot x\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(y))-2{x}^{2}y \\  & =({e}^{xy}+y\cdot {e}^{xy}\cdot x\cdot 1)-2{x}^{2}y \\  & ={e}^{xy}+xy{e}^{xy}-2{x}^{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(1,1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y}{|}_{(1,1)} & ={e}^{1\cdot 1}+1\cdot 1\cdot {e}^{1\cdot 1}-2\cdot {1}^{2}\cdot 1 \\  & =e+e-2 \\  & =2e-2\end{aligned}
$$
